non-host-reactively CD8+ Tc2 cells are capable of inhibiting marrow graft rejection without host reactivities, and thus, can facilitate engraftments across genetic barriers.

the development of novel immunotherapy strategies to enhance allogeneic marrow engraftment in the setting of reduced-intensity conditioning regimens.
the role of T cell subsets in the induction of graft rejection and GVHD.
the role of T cell subsets in the induction of GVHD and graft-versus-leukemia (GVL) effects after allogeneic bone marrow transplantation (BMT).

Tc2 type CD8+ T cell subsets can be manipulated to inhibit graft rejection and GVH without inducing GVHD.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tc1 and/or CD8 cells are necessary to inhibit graft rejection, and Tc2 and/or CD8 are necessary to reduce GVHD.

Tc2-type CD8 cells are the most potent subset to inhibit marrow graft rejection across genetic barriers, and that the non-host-reactive donor cells are capable of facilitating marrow engraftment with minimal risk for GVHD.
Tc2-type CD8+ T cell subsets can mediate alloengraftment without GVHD, and that this is a function of their ability to inhibit host-type precursor CTL and their lack of alloreactivity.
